content.description: Cross-sectional diagram showing driven gear body clearance measurement with directional arrows indicating measurement points

content.text: 1. CHECK BODY CLEARANCE OF DRIVEN GEAR
Push the driven gear to one side of the body. Using a feeler gauge, measure the clearance.
Standard body clearance: 0.07 — 0.15 mm (0.0028 — 0.059 in.)
Maximum body clearance: 0.3 mm (0.012 in.)
If the body clearance is greater than the maximum, replace the drive gear, driven gear or pump body.

content.description: Cross-sectional diagram showing tip clearance measurement between gear teeth and crescent-shaped pump body

content.text: 2. CHECK TIP CLEARANCE OF BOTH GEARS
Measure between the gear teeth and the crescent-shaped part of the pump body.
Standard tip clearance: 0.11 — 0.14 mm (0.0043 — 0.0055 in.)
Maximum tip clearance: 0.3 mm (0.012 in.)
If the tip clearance is greater than the maximum, replace the drive gear, driven gear or pump body.

content.description: Diagram showing measurement of side clearance using a steel straightedge and feeler gauge across the pump body and gears

content.text: 3. CHECK SIDE CLEARANCE OF BOTH GEARS
Using a steel straightedge and a feeler gauge, measure the side clearance of both gears.
Standard side clearance: 0.02 — 0.05 mm (0.0008 — 0.0020 in.)
Maximum side clearance: 0.1 mm (0.004 in.)
If the side clearance is greater than the maximum, replace the drive gear, driven gear or pump body.

content.description: Diagram showing hands using a screwdriver to pry off the front oil seal from the pump body

content.text: 4. INSPECT FRONT OIL SEAL
Check for wear, damage or cracks.
5. IF NECESSARY, REPLACE FRONT OIL SEAL
(a) Pry off the oil seal with a screwdriver.

content.description: Diagram showing installation of new oil seal using SST (Special Service Tool) and hammer, with the SST positioned on top of the seal being driven into the pump body

content.text: (b) Using SST and a hammer, install a new oil seal. The seal end should be flush with the outer edge of the pump body.
